title: Manifestation of the Glory of God
excerpt: Pst. Kiseku Muange’s Sunday Service message from Isaiah 60:1: the Word brings light, light brings revelation, revelation brings transformation, and Christ in us becomes the manifestation of God’s glory.
content:
“Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon you.” — Isaiah 60:1

Manifestation of the Glory of God

Our Sunday Service on 6 September 2026 carried the theme “Manifestation of the Glory of God.” Ministering from Isaiah 60:1, Pst. Kiseku Muange called the church to understand what it means for the light of God to come, for His glory to be revealed, and for the life of Christ to become visible through the believer.

The message began with a repeated declaration: “Arise, shine, for your light has come.” The emphasis was not that the believer must first manufacture light, but that God has already provided the light by which we are able to shine.

Light Has Come: The Word Has Come

Psalm 119:105 describes the Word of God as a lamp to our feet and a light to our path. Proverbs 6:23 likewise declares that the commandment is a lamp and the law is light.

From these Scriptures came one of the central declarations of the message:

“Light has come. The Word has come.”

When God's Word enters a situation, it brings direction where there was uncertainty and hope where there was hopelessness. The congregation was reminded that every problem has an answer in Jesus and that the Word of God can speak directly into the situations for which we have been waiting for an answer.

There Was Confusion Until the Word Came

Genesis 1:2–3 provided a picture of this truth. The earth was without form and void, and darkness covered the deep. Then God spoke: “Let there be light.”

The turning point was the Word of God.

Darkness did not have the final word. Confusion did not have the final word. Formlessness did not have the final word. God spoke, and light came.

“I will not be hopeless, because I have the Word of God.”

The church was encouraged to release and receive God's Word over circumstances that appear dark or without direction. When the Word comes, light comes.

Jesus Is the Living Word

The message then moved to John 1:1: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”

Jesus is not merely associated with the Word; He is the Living Word and the revelation of the invisible God. To need the Word is ultimately to need Christ.

This produced a clear progression throughout the sermon:

THE WORD → LIGHT → REVELATION → TRANSFORMATION

The Word produces light. Light brings revelation. Revelation produces transformation.

“The Word produces light in our lives. The Word produces revelation. Revelation produces transformation.”

The Christian life is therefore not meant to stop at hearing information. The Word received and revealed should transform the person who hears it.

From Light to Glory

Isaiah 60:1 does not end with light. It continues into glory: “and the glory of the LORD is risen upon you.”

The sermon described glory through ideas such as splendor, majesty, honor, power and presence. God's glory is not merely something to discuss; His manifest presence changes people and circumstances.

Moses' prayer in Exodus 33:18 captured this hunger:

“Please, show me Your glory.”

What Moses longed to see points us toward Christ, the One through whom the invisible God is revealed.

Christ in Me, the Hope of Glory

Colossians 1:27 became another major foundation of the message:

“Christ in you, the hope of glory.”

The glory of God is not presented only as an external experience for the believer to observe. Christ dwells in the believer, and the life of Jesus is to become manifest through us.

The message repeatedly returned to the truth that in Him we live, move and have our being. The same Christ who ministered in power is the Christ whom believers have received.

This led to perhaps the clearest definition of the sermon:

“In short, manifesting the glory is looking like Christ.”

Manifesting Glory Means Looking Like Christ

Manifestation is therefore bigger than displaying power. It includes the character, life, presence and power of Christ becoming visible through a believer.

The sermon developed into this progression:

WORD → LIGHT → REVELATION → TRANSFORMATION → CHRIST IN US → GLORY → MANIFESTATION

When Christ is revealed in us, our lives should increasingly point people toward Him. The believer carries a responsibility not merely to speak about Jesus, but to allow the life of Jesus to be made manifest.

The Glory Must Go Beyond the Church Doors

The message then widened from personal transformation to God's purpose for the world. The earth is to be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.

That means manifestation cannot end inside a Sunday service.

“Manifest God's glory outside the church doors.”

Students were challenged to carry Christ into their classes, professions, careers, businesses and everyday relationships. The world should encounter the brightness of Christ through transformed believers.

The Word transforms us, and transformed people become witnesses through whom others can encounter Christ.

Glory in Work, Career and Enterprise

The message also applied manifestation to practical life. God's glory should be visible not only in prayer and worship but also in excellence, work, creativity, career and enterprise.

One declaration captured the call to greater capacity:

“We are not only going to be employed; we are going to employ.”

Believers were encouraged to trust God, develop what He has placed in their hands and refuse to separate faith from the practical responsibilities of life.

Believe

Again and again, the message returned to faith. With God all things are possible. The congregation was challenged not to allow hopelessness, present circumstances or apparent limitations to become greater than the Word God has spoken.

Faith receives the Word. The Word brings light. Light brings revelation. Revelation transforms. And the transformed believer manifests Christ.

A Church That Carries His Glory

As the service drew toward its response, the challenge was simple but weighty: receive Christ, believe His Word and allow His life to become visible through you.

The manifestation of God's glory is not reserved for a platform, a preacher or a church building. Christ in the believer is the hope of glory.

We arise and shine because our Light has come.

Light has come. The Word has come. Receive the revelation. Be transformed. Let Christ be seen through your life.

Scriptures from the Message

  • Isaiah 60:1 — Arise, shine; your light has come
  • Psalm 119:105 — The Word is a lamp and a light
  • Proverbs 6:23 — The commandment is a lamp and the law is light
  • Genesis 1:2–3 — God speaks light into darkness
  • John 1:1 — Jesus, the Living Word
  • Exodus 33:18 — Moses asks to see God's glory
  • Colossians 1:27 — Christ in you, the hope of glory
  • Acts 17:28 — In Him we live, move and have our being
  • Habakkuk 2:14 — The earth filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord
